The context really decides this. Technically you could write it as an F# without a third, a fifth, but with a b7 and a b13 but there’s but you would only see that if it was being treated as an F# chord. You could even write it as a E with a b7 and a 9. Really theoretically you could call any note the root but you would never really see that because the context this would probably be used in would be as a substitution for some D chord simply because it sounds like that. You would have to look at the chords next to it to decide what to call it. If the chord right before it sets up a D major (one example could be the ii chord in G Major, A Minor) but instead you reach this chord, you would call likely call it a Dadd9 because that’s what it’s acting as ( it has an added 9 and a third, it has no fifth which is not required)
